passage: Thursday night. I feel sick and I don't know why I still feel safe. Gopika gave me the window seat today and shared her chips because I laughed when she called Meera a name. Everyone else laughed, and Gopika smiled at me like I'd passed a test. I felt warm for about ten seconds, and then I saw Meera's face and my stomach dropped. I don't even dislike Meera. I just don't want to be the person Gopika picks next. But being safe shouldn't depend on hurting someone. Tomorrow I'm going to sit with Nisha and the library kids. Gopika will probably be cold to me, or worse. I'm scared of that. I'll speak to Ma'am if it gets bad. And I'm going to say sorry to Meera. — Sangeeta

qa.q: What did Gopika give Sangeeta after Sangeeta laughed?
qa.a: She gave Sangeeta the window seat and shared her chips.

qa.q: What mixed feelings does Sangeeta describe?
qa.a: Feeling safe and sick together. Sangeeta felt warm for ten seconds after being rewarded, then Sangeeta's stomach dropped on seeing Meera's face.
Sangeeta will sit with Nisha and the library kids, tell Ma'am if it gets bad and apologise to Meera, so as to stop taking part.

qa.q: How might Meera have felt seeing the others laugh?
qa.a: Hurt and alone, since Meera was the one called a name while everyone laughed.

grounding: A bully rewards Sangeeta for joining in; Sangeeta feels safe and sick, and writes about stepping away even at some risk.

passage:
Deepak ran the back benches of the Kasturba village school, and for three months Sangeeta had been his favourite. He saved her a seat, shared his mango pickle, and nobody teased her anymore. All she had to do was laugh when he called Radha "buffalo" and hold the notebook while he tore Radha's pages.
She felt safe. She also felt sick every evening.
On Monday, Deepak handed her a chalk piece. "Write it on Radha's desk. Your turn."
Sangeeta's hand trembled. She looked at Radha, head bent, shoulders tight.
She put the chalk down. "No. I'm not doing this anymore."
Deepak's eyes narrowed. "Then don't come crying when they start on you."
At lunch she sat alone, heart hammering. After school she went to Sunita teacher and told her everything, including her own part. The teacher listened and said, "Stepping away took courage. I'll speak to Deepak and his parents tomorrow morning, and I'll keep an eye on you both."

qa.q: What did Deepak share with Sangeeta?
How did Sangeeta feel about being Deepak's favourite?
qa.a: She felt safe but also sick with guilt every evening, knowing her safety came from hurting Radha.

qa.q: What did Sangeeta do that was brave and wise?
qa.a: She refused to write on Radha's desk, stepped away despite the risk, and told a teacher everything the same day, including her own part.

qa.q: What might Radha feel if she saw Sangeeta put the chalk down?
qa.a: Radha might feel surprised and a little hopeful that someone had finally refused to join in.

grounding: A teen rewarded as a bully's sidekick feels safe but sick, steps away despite the risk, and tells a teacher.

passage:
At his school in Birmingham, Rafael had been Chidi's sidekick since September. Being next to Chidi meant nobody touched him. It meant a seat at the good table and jokes shared just with him.
The price was small at first: laugh when Chidi mocked the new boy's accent. Film when Chidi knocked someone's lunch off the table. Rafael always did.
On Thursday Chidi said, "Tell everyone Kwame wets his bed. Post it. You're good at that stuff."
Rafael's stomach turned. He liked Kwame. They'd done a science project together.
"I'm not posting that," he said.
Chidi laughed. "You'll be next, then."
Rafael walked out of the canteen, legs shaking. He knew what he was risking. But he couldn't keep buying safety by hurting other people.
After school he found the head of year, Mr Hughes, and told him about Chidi, and about his own part. Mr Hughes said, "That took guts, Rafael. We'll deal with this properly, starting today."

qa.q: Who had Rafael done a science project with?
How did Rafael feel when Chidi asked him to post the lie?
qa.a: His stomach turned; he felt sick and conflicted, liking Kwame and not wanting to hurt him.
Refusing to post the lie and telling Mr Hughes, including his own part, because safety shouldn't depend on hurting others.

qa.q: How does Chidi react to Rafael's refusal?
qa.a: Chidi laughs and threatens that Rafael will be next, showing he rewards loyalty and punishes anyone who steps away.

grounding: A teen rewarded as a bully's sidekick feels safe and sick, then refuses to join in, steps away and reports it.
